name: Cho'Gath
notes: Casts go one at a time: a cast takes effect as it starts and then keeps Cho'Gath busy for its cast time (no other cast, no attack) — Feast 0.25 s, Rupture 0.5 s, Feral Scream 0.5 s; Vorpal Spikes has no cast time but still cannot start inside another cast's busy window.

Opens with Feast (R) at t = 0 for its true-damage burst (the engine primes Spellblade and holds the first attack for its opening cast); Rupture (Q) then Feral Scream (W) follow as soon as the previous cast's busy time is over, and both are then recast on cooldown for the rest of the fight; Feast is likewise recast every time its long cooldown (60-80 s) comes back up.

Rupture's damage does not land with the cast: the dossier states its 0.625 s rupture delay is separate from and additional to the 0.5 s cast time, so Rupture's magic damage is scheduled as an event at cast-start + 0.5 s (cast time) + 0.625 s (delay); the cooldown starts at the cast, and the area still ruptures even though nothing else changes about that.

Feral Scream's damage is dealt as its cast starts (the wiki's 'effect at cast time end' is that same 0.5 s cast time, not a further delay, per the guide's reading), then its 0.5 s cast time keeps Cho'Gath busy.

Feast's damage is dealt as its cast starts, then its 0.25 s cast time keeps Cho'Gath busy; it uses the champion true-damage formula (base + 50% AP + 10% bonus health) since the dummy counts as an enemy champion, never the separate 1200 non-champion base.

Vorpal Spikes is cast right after an attack lands (for its own attack-timer reset) whenever it is off cooldown and not already armed; since attacks never land during another ability's busy window, this automatically respects the one-cast-at-a-time rule without an extra check. Its 3 charges then ride the next 3 attacks as on-hit magic damage scaling off the target's max health (champion, uncapped formula, not the reduced monster cap); the cooldown only starts once the charges are used or the 6 s window lapses.

Assumes 0 permanent Feast stacks: nothing forces a pre-fight kill for a level-16 Cho'Gath entering this fight, so neither the extra bonus health, the wiki's +8/12/16-per-stack Feast damage, nor Vorpal Spikes' +0.5%-per-stack term are added; Vorpal Spikes' listed target-max-health percentages already are the 0-stack values.
Carnivore (P) only triggers on a kill, which never happens against a stationary dummy with a large health pool, so it contributes nothing and is omitted.
Crowd control (the knock-up, the silence, both slows) is ignored, as instructed: none of it affects a stationary, non-attacking dummy.
Mana costs are not modeled: nothing here binds across a 15 s fight at level 16.
